provenance.instrument: West Manchester Township Code Chapter 150 Zoning (Ord. No. 79-1, 1-4-1979, amended in its entirety by Ord. No. 87-2, 3-31-1987, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-11-13 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 26-01 (2026-01-05, Non-Uniformed Employees Pension Plan, Chapter 29), 26-02 (2026-01-22, Vehicles and Traffic, 139-323) and 26-03 (2026-05-28, Subdivision and Land Development, Chapter 121). provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-11-13'. The definitions show amendments through Ord. No. 25-06 (10-23-2025). The three 2026 New Laws amend Chapters 29, 139 and 121, not the zoning chapter (New Laws search).
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, accessory apartment, in-law, ECHO or similar rule. 'The uses shown as permitted in each zone are the only uses permitted in that zone' (150-8). Only one principal use per lot (150-12.1)

A house with a second dwelling unit is a duplex: 'A freestanding building containing two dwelling units for two families arranged in a side-by-side or over-and-under configuration' (150-5). The single-family zones (A, R, R-1, R-2, R-3, R-5, OSR-1, OSR-2, OSR-3) do not list duplexes, so a second unit there needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board

In R-6 duplex dwellings are permitted by right: lot 4,000 sq ft, width 40 ft, depth 100 ft, front 20 ft, side 8 ft, rear 15 ft, buildings at most 50% (150-75B, 150-78). That covers a unit in or attached to the house. A unit in a separate building is not a duplex and needs a use variance in every zone. Duplexes are also permitted in R-4 (7,260 sq ft per unit, 150-60, 150-63) and in the designated residential area of a planned MU development (150-116.2A, 150-116.4E)

Some read 150-9 ('Any use not specifically allowed elsewhere in this chapter shall be allowed by special exception ...') as a special exception path for a second unit. Since the code defines and allows duplexes elsewhere, that reading is doubtful. Confirm with the Zoning Officer that a second unit in a single-family zone is treated as a duplex (use variance) everywhere except R-6

Two-family conversion of a detached single-family dwelling is a special exception only in the Local Commercial (LC) Zone: lot 8,000 sq ft, public sewer and water, no outside change except fire escapes (150-85D, 150-354). LC also permits 'One dwelling unit, in conjunction with another permitted use' inside the same building (150-83F, 150-86). Single-family detached dwellings are not a listed LC use

Off-street parking: single-family dwellings on their own lots are exempt (150-244). Other residential dwellings need 2 spaces per dwelling unit (150-263), so a duplex or a two-family conversion needs 4
Converting a single-family detached dwelling into not more than three units is not land development under the subdivision ordinance (121-6)

'Lot coverage' in the A, R, R-1, R-2, R-3, OSR and LC zones (and R-5 without public sewer and water) is impervious cover: buildings, driveways, parking and sidewalks (150-5). R-5 and R-6 with both services cap the principal building (building coverage), with accessory uses together at most 20% (150-73C, 150-80C)

No accessory use (except permitted signs) in the front yard in A, R, R-1, R-2, R-3, R-6 and the OSR zones. Accessory buildings 15 ft high (20 ft in R-1 and R-2) (150-20D, 150-29B, 150-30B, 150-38B, 150-39B, 150-47B, 150-48B, 150-56B, 150-57B, 150-73, 150-80, 150-228.5D, 150-228.11D, 150-228.17D)

Front setback averaging: where at least two adjacent buildings within 100 ft are closer to the street, their average is the front setback, never less than 25 ft (150-238A). An existing lot below the zone's lot area or width may be used for a permitted use if it meets the setbacks (150-243)
The zone list names an (H) Historical Zone overlay (150-6), but Chapter 150 has no Historical Zone article. No historic path
Every dwelling unit at least 700 sq ft of habitable floor area for a single-family, duplex or townhouse unit, 350 sq ft for a one-person efficiency (150-235)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: West Manchester Township (York County) Zoning Officer. Read on eCode360 (WE1311) in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, 'family dwelling', relative, 'housekeeping unit', caretaker, 'tenant house' and 'guest house' found no ADU text. A second search for conversion, two-family, duplex, 'accessory residential' and 'second dwelling' found 150-354 (LC two-family conversions), duplex standards in R-4, R-6 and MU, and two-family dwellings in the Planned Residential Development Overlay. Read in full: Article II definitions, Article III zones, Article IV general use regulations, the A, R, R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, LC, MU, OSR-1, OSR-2 and OSR-3 zones, Article XXIII supplementary regulations and Article XXIV parking. Not read: HC, PO, RC, I-1, I-2, I-3, OS, Q, DCO, PRD (search excerpts only) and the special exception criteria (150-302, 150-357.1). Fix round 2026-11-14 after an independent review: headline path set to a use variance (second unit read as a duplex under 150-5 and 150-8), 150-9 kept as a disputed side note, 2026 caution removed (the New Laws amend Chapters 29, 139 and 121), R-5 utility rows completed, impervious lot coverage noted, OSR rows and parking added.

term.note: No ADU term. Searched for accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, in-law, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, family dwelling, relative, housekeeping unit, caretaker, tenant house, guest house, conversion, two-family and duplex.

status.note: The single-family zones list single-family detached dwellings and incidental accessory uses. 'The uses shown as permitted in each zone are the only uses permitted in that zone' (150-8). Only one principal use per lot (150-12.1).

path.note: A house with a second dwelling unit is a duplex by definition ('two dwelling units for two families', 150-5). Duplexes are not a permitted use in the single-family zones, and 'The uses shown as permitted in each zone are the only uses permitted in that zone' (150-8). So a second unit needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). In R-6 a duplex is permitted by right on 4,000 sq ft (150-78). A unit in a separate building is not a duplex (one freestanding building), so it needs a use variance in every zone. Side note, disputed: 150-9 allows by special exception 'Any use not specifically allowed elsewhere in this chapter'. A duplex is allowed elsewhere, so that path likely does not reach a second unit. Confirm with the Zoning Officer.

fallback_path.note: Relief from a zone rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family conversion of a detached single-family dwelling
value.conditions: Minimum lot area 8,000 sq ft. Public sewer and water. No change to the outside look except fire escapes. All floors above grade with direct escape to ground level. 2 parking spaces per dwelling unit (150-263). For an existing single-family detached dwelling (not a listed LC use).
value.note: Zoning Hearing Board special exception. The former four-space parking rule was repealed (Ord. No. 01-03). Converting a house into not more than three units is not land development (121-6).

value.name: Duplex dwelling in R-6
value.conditions: Duplex dwellings are a permitted use. Lot 4,000 sq ft, width 40 ft, depth 100 ft, front 20 ft, side 8 ft, rear 15 ft, height 35 ft, the principal building at most 50% of the lot. 2 parking spaces per dwelling unit (150-263).
value.note: A house with a second unit side by side or over and under is a duplex (150-5), so in R-6 this is the by-right way to add a unit, on a lot that meets the duplex standards. Converting a house into not more than three units is not land development (121-6). Only for a unit in or attached to the house. A unit in a separate building is not a duplex.

value.name: Duplex dwelling in R-4
value.conditions: Duplex dwellings are a permitted use. 7,260 sq ft per dwelling unit, width 55 ft, depth 120 ft, front 35 ft, side 25 ft, rear 35 ft, 35 ft, lot coverage 40%. Single-family detached dwellings are not listed in R-4. 2 parking spaces per dwelling unit (150-263).
value.note: Lot figure is two units at 7,260 sq ft each.

value.name: Duplex dwelling in the MU Zone
value.conditions: Duplex dwellings in a designated residential development area of a planned mixed-use development on at least 100 contiguous acres under one owner, with public water and sewer. Lot 4,000 sq ft (2,000 per unit, at most 8 units an acre), width 40 ft, depth 100 ft, front 20 ft, side 8 ft (end units), rear 15 ft, 35 ft, lot coverage 60%.
